title: Verdict system — how your calls count
detail: When you say 'ye this feels good' mid-session, does that count as an official decision, or only after a proper rested session? Two-tier = quick calls count immediately as decisions, and feel-things additionally get one final rested yes/no later. Strict = only rested-session calls ever count. All-count = every clear-headed call counts, whenever made. Under every option, marathon sessions and cheated runs (god mode / slow-mo / live edits) stay unofficial. Also updates what 'rested' means to fit your 15:00-23:00 work shift: it goes by how long you've been awake and playing, not the wall clock — home at midnight is your late afternoon.

title: Reactive as DodgeBot policy of record
unblocks: the wolf-fight question + fresh proof baseline
detail: The dodge-proof bot has two brains. The old cautious one treats wolves as 'never go near them' and fails three wolf fights a human can actually dodge fine. The new REACTIVE brain walks into range and dodges the attack windups like a human — it passes all three cleanly, and it is still honest (it fails the deliberately-impossible test). YES = reactive becomes the official tester, the three old failures become explained history, and I re-run every proof to set the new baseline. NO = keep the cautious brain as official and the wolf-fight failures stay open questions.

title: Tester recruitment sizing
detail: How many outside playtesters do we recruit for Gate 1? Strangers take calendar time to find, so this number decides how soon Gate 1 can even be scheduled. The drafted proposal: 10-16 people total, at least 4 complete strangers per test cycle, and at least 5 fresh people held back for cycle 2 (so the second round isn't all veterans).

title: Export pipeline (last M7 item)
detail: Say DO IT and I build the last remaining M7 piece: the script that packages the game into a zip people can download and run. Two flavors — a dev build with everything unlocked, and a tester build with the cheats stripped (god mode, slow-mo, debug console, live stat editing all removed). The design is already written and approved-shaped; this is just the go-ahead. Runs without you.

title: Stand up itch + devlog + Discord
unblocks: anywhere for testers to come from
detail: Create the three public places testers will come from: an itch.io page for the game, a devlog thread, and a bare-bones Discord. Open since M3 — the plan put them early on purpose so there's a runway of people watching before we ever ask anyone to play. The assessment ranked this the single biggest risk to Gate 1. Roughly one evening, and it's accounts + posting, so it's yours.

If that machine dies, we cannot rebuild the art pack. Find which machine has it and push. Ten minutes; cheapest insurance in the project.

Check the two speed presets ([ and ]), how the ranger faces, pause freezing absolutely everything (Esc), the two camera-smoothing modes (I), and especially walking tight against walls and props — the thing that used to stick and shiver. You said 'doesnt lag anymore', but that was a tired-session note; this rested word is what formally closes milestone M2.

title: Six ordinaries ratification
detail: Play against all six regular enemies rested and give the official word: wolf (melee slash), skeleton archer (aimed shots), fanmaw (shot fans — its orbs got bigger recently, re-feel it), ringer (ring bursts while it chases), leadshot (the sniper that aims where you're GOING), blightcaster (lingering poison zones). You've liked them all in quick reactions ('he does exactly that!'), but 'Approved' was never formally said.

title: Weekly GIF
detail: One 30-60 second gameplay GIF posted to the devlog + one community, every week, no exceptions — it's how testers find the game before we ask anyone to play. Press G in-game to dump the last 10 seconds, tools/gif.ps1 converts (or hand it to the session). #2 material: the boss fight, the new enemies in the dusk town, the generated world.

title: Nine-row acceptance — eye rows
detail: A 15-minute picture check, rested. Open the sign-off sheet (game notes/NINE_ROW_ACCEPTANCE.md) plus the three stress-test screenshots in reports/ (normal, minimum-settings, and colorblind-simulation — attach them to this card if you like) and judge with your eyes: enemy shots always visible over your own effects? Your shots clearly quieter than theirs? Enemy vs friendly unmistakable at max chaos, including in the colorblind shot? Arena floors calm? Nothing strobing? Fill the table at the bottom. The other rows are machine-checked already.

title: CORE-34 no-ability clear
unblocks: proof no fight needs the ability
detail: Play one full scenario (second_contact or first_contact suggested) start to clean finish WITHOUT ever pressing Space (the ability key). This proves the design rule that movement alone is always enough — no fight secretly requires the ability. Tired counts; it's evidence, not feel. I verify the logs afterward.

title: Grass slits — the 13 sealed cells
detail: In the generated town, 13 narrow gaps between houses are currently walled off. They were sealed because walking into them made you slide UNDER overlapping house sprites — it looked broken. Keep sealed = safest, town slightly less open. Reopen = more open town, but that broken-looking slide returns in exactly those gaps. Third option = ask the tile tool for proper 'blocked ground' art there (fixes both, someday, needs upstream art).

title: Warden HP vs the 13-second line
detail: The design doc says the boss should survive roughly 13 seconds of your best weapon's sustained damage. Measured today he actually dies in 8.4 seconds — the doc was written against older weapon numbers. Accept = 8.4 s is fine as-is, fix the doc to match. Raise = bump his health to ~575 so he lasts ~13 s again (I re-run his dodge proofs after). Your other two weapons already sit near 13 s for comparison.

title: Fanmaw projectile hue — orange vs teal
detail: Fanmaw's shots are orange. For red-green colorblind players that orange lands in the same muddy 'olive' bucket as the skeleton archer's red — two different enemies' shots can read samey. Teal is the safe alternative; either way it's a one-line file change. Look at the colorblind-simulation screenshot in reports/ (attach it to this card — it IS the evidence) and pick.

title: Scarecrow:strawfield for the Warden
detail: The boss currently wears the scarecrow sprite from your catalog as a stand-in. Keep it? Or name any other character from the catalog — either way it's a one-line change, and when you draw polished boss art later it drops into the same slot with zero code.

title: Eyes-closed audio sanity (Law 7)
detail: One mixed fight with your eyes closed: can you tell the seven warning sounds apart (ranged windup, melee windup, zone cast, zone armed, boss phase change, you got hit, you died)? The design law says sound must work as a second channel when your eyes are busy. Write the verdict + date in the slot at the bottom of game notes/AUDIO_CUE_MAP.md. Tired counts.

title: Audio cues in normal play
detail: While playing normally (rested): do the placeholder sounds feel right — helpful, not annoying, not drowning anything out? The eyes-closed test checks whether you CAN hear them; this one checks whether you WANT to.
